<reason>CON won by holding the motion's condition: comparable integration removes one objection but does not prove family priority. A reframed the tradeoff as resident reunion vs other residents' care, exposed double-counting of retention, answered mobility with expected benefit vs guarantee, and drew a principled dependency line while PRO's fungibility claim named alternatives without proving they meet the need.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's resident-vs-resident reframe plus inconsistency charge: pay/training/temporary visas are possible not proven substitutes, and PRO cannot attack guestworker insecurity then rely on temporary recruitment while calling a permanent nurse non-membership.</best_rebuttal>
